ref.title: Agents in Microsoft Foundry

cheatsheet.title: Define a prompt agent with tools (Python)
cheatsheet.code:
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.ai.projects.models import PromptAgentDefinition, FunctionTool, MCPTool

project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=PROJECT_ENDPOINT, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
func = FunctionTool(
    name="get_order", description="Get an order by ID.", strict=True,
    parameters={"type": "object",
                "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
                "required": ["order_id"], "additionalProperties": False})
mcp = MCPTool(
    server_label="github", server_url="https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp",
    allowed_tools=["search_issues"], require_approval="always",
    project_connection_id="my-mcp-connection")
agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="support-agent",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(
        model="gpt-5-mini", instructions="Use tools when needed.", tools=[func, mcp]))
cheatsheet.note: `create_version` + `PromptAgentDefinition`, never `create_agent`. Function schema: `strict=True` goes with `additionalProperties: False` and a `required` list. MCP: unique `server_label`, remote `server_url`, `allowed_tools` (omitted = all tools; current docs add that `[]` also means all), `require_approval` (default `always`; also `never` or per-tool `always`/`never` lists), credentials through `project_connection_id`.

ref.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

cheatsheet.title: Run it: conversation + tool-call loop (Python)
cheatsheet.code:
import json
openai_client = project.get_openai_client()
ref = {"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}}
conv = openai_client.conversations.create()
resp = openai_client.responses.create(
    conversation=conv.id, input="Where is order 1182?", extra_body=ref)
replies = []
for item in resp.output:
    if item.type == "function_call":            # your app runs the function
        result = get_order(**json.loads(item.arguments))
        replies.append({"type": "function_call_output",
                        "call_id": item.call_id, "output": json.dumps(result)})
    elif item.type == "mcp_approval_request":   # human approval gate
        replies.append({"type": "mcp_approval_response",
                        "approval_request_id": item.id, "approve": True})
if replies:
    resp = openai_client.responses.create(
        conversation=conv.id, input=replies, extra_body=ref)
cheatsheet.note: Exam era (SDK 2.0.x): `get_openai_client()` plus `extra_body={"agent_reference": ...}`; samples of that era often sent the follow-up with `previous_response_id=response.id`, and the Learn training modules still show the older key `agent`. Docs today: `project.get_openai_client(agent_name=...)` and follow-ups in the same conversation. Return all tool outputs in one call. Function outputs are due within 10 minutes of run creation; non-streaming MCP calls time out at 100 seconds.

Preferences and facts recalled in later conversations. Not a transcript

The 60-day figure isn't confirmed for the April 2026 docs.

cheatsheet.title: Tool picker: need -> tool -> gotcha
rows: Run your own code, or reach systems only your app can reach
Function calling (`FunctionTool`)
Executed by your app: `function_call` -> `function_call_output` with `call_id`; outputs due within 10 minutes of run creation; the portal can't add or edit function definitions
Q&A over uploaded files without managing search
File search (`FileSearchTool`)

`openai_client.vector_stores.create()` + `files.upload_and_poll()`; 512 MB per file; 10,000 files per vector store; one vector store per agent; hybrid search and reranking built in; a standard setup keeps files in your Storage account and Azure AI Search service
Ground on an existing Azure AI Search index
Azure AI Search tool (`AzureAISearchTool`)

`project_connection_id` + `index_name`; `query_type`: `simple`, `semantic`, `vector`, `vector_simple_hybrid` (hybrid vector + keyword), `vector_semantic_hybrid` (hybrid + semantic ranker); `top_k`; optional `filter`; one index per tool; a search service with public access disabled needs a managed identity (keyless) connection and a standard setup with VNet injection. Docs today (Nov 2026) title the page Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search) index
Shared multi-source knowledge with agentic retrieval and permission trimming
Foundry IQ knowledge base through `MCPTool`

`server_url` = `{search_endpoint}/knowledgebases/{kb}/mcp?api-version=...`; `allowed_tools=["knowledge_base_retrieve"]`; `RemoteTool` connection with `ProjectManagedIdentity`; the project identity needs Search Index Data Reader on the Azure AI Search service; per-user trimming via `x-ms-query-source-authorization`
Current public web information
Web search (`WebSearchTool`)

No Bing resource or connection needed; data leaves the Azure compliance boundary; restrict to chosen public domains with Grounding with Bing Custom Search (preview); the explicit Grounding with Bing Search tool (`bing_grounding`) needs a Bing project connection
Call an existing REST API from its spec
OpenAPI tool (`OpenApiTool`)

OpenAPI 3.0/3.1; each operation needs an `operationId` (letters, `-`, `_` only); auth: anonymous, API key held in a project connection (key name must match the spec's security scheme), or managed identity with the API's audience; no OAuth identity passthrough
Tools hosted on a remote MCP server

`server_label` (unique per agent), `server_url`, `allowed_tools`, `require_approval`, `project_connection_id`; remote endpoints only (host local servers on Container Apps or Functions); non-streaming calls time out at 100 seconds
Python sandbox for analysis and charts

Extra per-session charge; a session lasts 1 hour with a 30-minute idle timeout; generated files come back as `container_file_citation` annotations
Delegate to another agent in any framework

Project connection for the remote A2A endpoint + a tool that references it with `project_connection_id`; replaces classic connected agents. Exam era: preview (`A2APreviewTool`, type `a2a_preview`). Docs today: GA `A2ATool` (August 2026); a Foundry agent target needs incoming A2A enabled and the Foundry Agent Consumer role for the caller
Per-user personalization across sessions

Needs a memory store and a `scope`; see the memory section
SharePoint content with each user's permissions

Identity passthrough (on-behalf-of) with a user identity only; Microsoft 365 Copilot license or pay-as-you-go; one SharePoint tool per agent; same tenant; doesn't work once the agent is published to Teams
Queue-triggered serverless logic

Input and output Storage queue bindings; standard agent setup only; Storage Queue Data Contributor for the project and function app identities; taught in the Learn custom-tools module
A web UI or desktop app with no API
Browser automation / Computer use

Browser automation drives a managed Playwright Workspaces browser; Computer use returns `computer_call` actions that YOUR app executes and answers with `computer_call_output` plus a screenshot. Both were preview in the exam era; docs today show them as generally available
Generate images in a conversation
Image generation tool (preview)
Needs a `gpt-image-1` deployment plus an orchestrator model in the same project; pass the header `x-ms-oai-image-generation-deployment`

After the April 2026 outline: Toolbox (one MCP endpoint that bundles tools; preview from April 20, stable July 2026), the Fabric data agent tool deprecated in favor of Fabric IQ (November 2026), and Azure AI Search branded Foundry IQ (November 2026).

cheatsheet.title: Agent memory (preview) essentials
bullets: Long-term memory, not chat history: the service extracts, consolidates, and retrieves facts across conversations. Use a knowledge base for curated organizational content and file search for user-provided documents.

A memory store needs a chat model deployment and an embedding model deployment: `project.beta.memory_stores.create(name=..., definition=MemoryStoreDefaultDefinition(chat_model=..., embedding_model=..., options=MemoryStoreDefaultOptions(...)))`.

Exam era (Apr 2026): two memory types - user profile and chat summary (`user_profile_enabled`, `chat_summary_enabled`), tuned with `user_profile_details`. Docs today add procedural memory, a default TTL, and item-level create/update/delete (SDK 2.2.0, May 2026, and later).
Attach to a prompt agent with `MemorySearchPreviewTool(memory_store_name=..., scope=..., update_delay=...)` (tool type `memory_search_preview`). The tool both reads and writes memories.

`scope` partitions memories. `{{$userId}}` is resolved per request from the caller's Microsoft Entra identity (tenant ID + object ID); a static scope is shared by everyone who uses it. Docs today also accept an `x-memory-user-id` request header for back ends that call on behalf of users (not confirmed for the exam era).
`update_delay` debounces writes until the conversation has been inactive; default 300 seconds. The low-level `begin_update_memories(..., update_delay=0)` writes immediately.
Low-level APIs (`search_memories`, `begin_update_memories`, `delete_scope`) need an explicit `scope`; `delete_scope` removes one user's memories.
Limits (docs today): 100 scopes per store, 10,000 memories per scope, no virtual network support.
cheatsheet.note: A back end that calls with one shared identity puts every customer in the same `{{$userId}}` scope unless it supplies a per-user scope (or, in docs today, the `x-memory-user-id` header).

ref.title: Microsoft Agent Framework workflow orchestrations

cheatsheet.title: Safeguards and approval controls
bullets: MCP `require_approval`: `always` (default), `never`, or per-tool lists (`{"never": [...]}` or `{"always": [...]}`). A gated call surfaces as `mcp_approval_request`; answer with `mcp_approval_response` (`approval_request_id`, `approve`), continuing the same conversation or response chain.
Limit the blast radius with `allowed_tools`; when it is omitted, every tool on the server is available.

Function tools run in your app, so validate arguments and confirm with the user before side effects. Agent Framework tools can require approval (`approval_mode="always_require"` on the tool decorator).
Foundry workflows (preview): human in the loop = ask a question, wait for input, branch with if/else. Agent Framework Magentic can require human plan review.

Guardrails on agents (preview): intervention points are user input, tool call, tool response, and output. The agent's guardrail fully overrides the model deployment's guardrail; an agent with none assigned inherits the model deployment's.
Agents support only the annotate-and-block action; Groundedness and Spotlighting controls don't apply to agents.
Treat tool descriptions and tool outputs as untrusted input (indirect prompt injection); keep secrets out of prompts, tool outputs, and traces.
Least privilege for the identity a tool uses (agent identity or project managed identity); keep shared credentials in project connections.
cheatsheet.note: Semi-autonomous design = no approval for read-only tools (`never`), approval for write or delete tools (`always`). Tool call and tool response content is scanned only if the agent's guardrail defines controls for those intervention points.

cheatsheet.title: Trace, monitor, evaluate agents
rows: See every model and tool step without code changes
Server-side tracing
Connect Application Insights to the project; automatic for prompt and hosted agents; the Traces tab keeps 90 days; viewers need Log Analytics Reader
Trace your own app code around agent calls
Client-side tracing (preview)

Set `AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING=true` before `AIProjectInstrumentor().instrument()`; export with `configure_azure_monitor(connection_string=project.telemetry.get_application_insights_connection_string())`
Capture prompts and tool arguments in spans
Content recording
Off by default; development only. Exam-era variable: `AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED=true`. Docs today: `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true`
Find the failing step
Span tree
`invoke_agent` with `execute_tool` child spans; attributes `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and `gen_ai.tool.call.result`; search by response ID or trace ID
Operational health
Agent monitoring dashboard (Monitor tab)
Token usage, latency, run success rate, evaluation scores, red teaming results
Did it understand the user and follow instructions?
System evaluators
Intent Resolution, Task Adherence, Task Completion, Task Navigation Efficiency (needs expected actions)
Did it use tools correctly?
Process evaluators
Tool Call Accuracy, Tool Selection, Tool Input Accuracy, Tool Output Utilization, Tool Call Success
Score production traffic as responses complete
Continuous evaluation rule

`EvaluationRule` with event type `RESPONSE_COMPLETED` and an agent-name filter (default cap 100 runs per hour); the project managed identity needs Azure AI User (renamed Foundry User later in 2026). Scheduled `TIMER_TRIGGER` rules were added in November 2026
Test an agent before release
Agent-targeted evaluation
`evals.runs.create` with data source `azure_ai_target_completions` and target type `azure_ai_agent`; map `{{sample.output_items}}` (includes tool calls) or `{{sample.output_text}}`
cheatsheet.note: 429 `rate_limit_exceeded` = the model deployment is throttling: retry with exponential backoff and jitter. Tool-related evaluators have limited support when the run includes Azure AI Search, Bing, SharePoint, Code Interpreter, Fabric, or web search calls.

flashcards.front: Default value of `require_approval` on an MCP tool?
flashcards.back: `always` - every call surfaces an `mcp_approval_request` until you set `never` or a per-tool list.

flashcards.front: MCP tool: what happens when `allowed_tools` is omitted?
flashcards.back: The agent can use ALL tools on the server; pass a list of names to restrict. Current docs add that `[]` also means all tools.

flashcards.front: How do you approve a pending MCP tool call?
flashcards.back: Send an `mcp_approval_response` item with `approval_request_id` (the request item's `id`) and `approve`, continuing the same conversation or chaining with `previous_response_id`.

flashcards.front: Which item do you send back after running a function tool?
flashcards.back: `function_call_output` with the `call_id` from the `function_call` item and a string `output`.

flashcards.front: Time limit for returning function tool outputs?
flashcards.back: The run expires 10 minutes after creation (total elapsed time, not per function).

flashcards.front: Which client creates conversations and responses for an agent?
flashcards.back: The OpenAI client from `project.get_openai_client()`; reference the agent with `extra_body={"agent_reference": {...}}`. The project client manages agents and versions.

flashcards.front: Classic -> current agent API: what replaced threads, runs, and `create_agent`?
Azure AI Search tool: which `query_type` is hybrid + semantic ranker, and which is hybrid without it?
flashcards.back: `vector_semantic_hybrid` vs `vector_simple_hybrid`. The tool targets exactly one index.

flashcards.front: File search limits per file, per vector store, per agent?
flashcards.back: 512 MB per file; 10,000 files per vector store; one vector store per agent (and one per conversation).

flashcards.front: Memory tool placeholder for a per-user scope?
flashcards.back: `{{$userId}}` - resolved from the caller's Entra tenant ID + object ID (docs today also read an `x-memory-user-id` header).

flashcards.front: Default `update_delay` of the memory search tool?
flashcards.back: 300 seconds of inactivity before memories are written.

flashcards.front: What does a memory store need at creation?
flashcards.back: A chat model deployment and an embedding model deployment.

flashcards.front: Maximum number of tools registered per agent?
flashcards.back: 128. (Docs today also cap an agent at 1,000 versions.)
The A2A tool (preview in the exam era, GA since August 2026), a workflow, or a Microsoft Agent Framework orchestration.

flashcards.front: What turns on server-side agent tracing?
flashcards.back: Connecting an Application Insights resource to the project - no code changes. Log Analytics Reader is needed to view traces.

flashcards.front: Evaluator for: did the agent follow its system instructions and constraints?
flashcards.back: Task Adherence (preview), a pass/fail system evaluator.

flashcards.front: An agent and its model deployment both have guardrails. Which applies?
flashcards.back: The agent's guardrail fully overrides the model's. With none assigned, the agent inherits the model deployment's guardrail.

flashcards.front: Power Fx variable prefixes in Foundry workflows?
flashcards.back: `System.` for system variables (for example `System.LastMessage.Text`) and `Local.` for local variables.

questions.stem: You are migrating a support bot from the classic threads-and-runs agent API to the current Foundry Agent Service API by using `azure-ai-projects` 2.x. The agent must be stored as a versioned prompt agent, and multi-turn history must be kept on the service. Complete the Python code.
questions.code:
project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=ENDPOINT, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
agent = project.agents.[[1]](
    agent_name="support-agent",
    definition=[[2]](
        model="gpt-5-mini",
        instructions="You answer product support questions.",
        tools=[FileSearchTool(vector_store_ids=[vector_store.id])],
    ),
)
openai_client = project.get_openai_client()
conversation = openai_client.[[3]].create()
response = openai_client.responses.create(
    conversation=conversation.id,
    input="How do I reset my router?",
    extra_body={"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}},
)
print(response.output_text)
questions.explanation: `create_agent()` belongs to the classic API and was removed in SDK 2.0; agents are created as immutable versions with `project.agents.create_version()` and a `PromptAgentDefinition` that holds the model, instructions, and tools. Conversations and responses are called on the OpenAI client returned by `project.get_openai_client()`, where conversations replace threads and responses replace runs. `HostedAgentDefinition` describes a containerized agent, not a declarative prompt agent. Since SDK 2.1.0 (April 20, 2026) the docs bind the agent with `get_openai_client(agent_name=...)` instead of `extra_body`.

questions.stem: A claims app calls a Foundry prompt agent through the Responses API by using the Python SDK. Compliance requires that the service doesn't persist prompts or responses. The app keeps its own encrypted transcript and must still support multi-turn dialogs. What should you do?
options: Create a conversation and pass its ID in `conversation` on every call
Pass `previous_response_id` from the prior turn on every call
Set `store=False` on every call and resend the earlier turns in `input`
Set `store=False` on every call and pass `previous_response_id`
questions.explanation: With `store=False` the service doesn't persist the response, so the application must carry the context forward by passing the earlier items as input on the next request. A conversation is a durable server-side object, and `previous_response_id` works only because responses are stored by default, so it has nothing to reference when `store` is `False`.

ref.title: Build with agents, conversations, and responses

questions.stem: You create a prompt agent by sending `POST {project_endpoint}/agents?api-version=v1`. The agent needs one custom function that your application executes, and the arguments that the model generates must adhere strictly to the schema. Complete the `definition` object of the request body.
questions.explanation: A declaratively defined agent uses `kind` set to `prompt`; `hosted` is for containerized agents that you deploy as an image. A custom function that your application runs is a tool of `type` `function` with a JSON Schema in `parameters`, whereas `openapi` and `mcp` tools are executed by the service against an API or a remote server. The documented strict sample closes the schema with the JSON Schema keyword `additionalProperties` set to false and lists the properties in `required`.

ref.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

questions.stem: A prompt agent has a `FunctionTool` named `get_order_status`. Your application must run the function locally when the agent requests it and then return the result so that the agent can produce its final answer. The follow-up request is chained to the first response. Complete the Python code.
questions.code:
agent_ref = {"agent_reference": {"name": agent.name, "type": "agent_reference"}}
response = openai_client.responses.create(
    input="Where is order 1182?", extra_body=agent_ref)
input_list = []
for item in response.output:
    if item.type == "function_call" and item.name == "get_order_status":
        result = get_order_status(**json.loads(item.[[1]]))
        input_list.append(FunctionCallOutput(
            type="[[2]]",
            [[3]]=item.call_id,
            output=json.dumps(result),
        ))
response = openai_client.responses.create(
    input=input_list,
    previous_response_id=response.id,
    extra_body=agent_ref,
)
print(response.output_text)
questions.explanation: Function tools run client-side: the response contains a `function_call` item whose `arguments` field is a JSON string. The application executes the function and sends a `function_call_output` item that echoes the `call_id`, before the run expires (10 minutes after creation). `tool_outputs` and `tool_call_id` belong to the classic runs API and Chat Completions, not to the Responses-based agent API. Current doc samples send the follow-up with `conversation=conversation.id` instead of `previous_response_id`; the items are the same.

ref.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

questions.stem: You add a custom `get_inventory` function to a prompt agent by using the Python SDK for the current Foundry Agent Service API. The function must run in your application. You have a list of possible actions, and not all of them are used. Which actions should you perform in sequence?
items: Create an agent version whose definition includes a `FunctionTool` with a JSON Schema for the parameters
Call `responses.create` with the user's question and a reference to the agent
Run `get_inventory` locally with the arguments from the `function_call` output item
Call `responses.create` again with a `function_call_output` item that has the matching `call_id`
distractors: Poll the run until its status is `requires_action`, and then call `submit_tool_outputs`
Upload the function's source file to the agent's Code Interpreter container
questions.explanation: Function tools are executed by your application: the agent version declares the tool, the first response returns a `function_call` item, your code runs the function, and a second `responses.create` call (in the same conversation or chained with `previous_response_id`) returns a `function_call_output` with the same `call_id`. Polling a run and submitting tool outputs to it is the classic threads-and-runs pattern, and Code Interpreter runs model-written code in a sandbox rather than hosting your function.

ref.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

questions.stem: A prompt agent has a function tool named `start_export`. When the agent requests the function, your application runs an export that takes about 25 minutes and then submits the result, but the submission fails because the request has expired. The export duration can't be reduced. What should you do?
options: Set `strict` to `true` in the function definition and resubmit the output
Return a job ID immediately and add a function that checks the job status
Set `tool_choice` to `required` when you create the first response
Submit the output by using `previous_response_id` instead of the conversation ID
questions.explanation: Function tool outputs must be submitted before the run expires, 10 minutes after it was created, and that limit covers total elapsed time rather than each function. For long operations the guidance is to return a status immediately and poll separately, for example through a second function. `strict` affects schema adherence, `tool_choice` controls whether a tool is called, and changing how context is chained doesn't extend the expiry.

ref.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

questions.stem: You add GitHub's remote MCP server to a prompt agent in Foundry Agent Service. The agent must be able to call only two read-only tools, those calls must run without pausing for human review, and the GitHub personal access token must be stored in the Foundry project rather than in the agent definition. Complete the tool definition.
questions.explanation: `allowed_tools` with a list of tool names restricts the agent to those tools; if it is omitted, every tool on the server is available. `require_approval` defaults to `always`, so it must be set to `never` to avoid `mcp_approval_request` pauses. `project_connection_id` points to a project connection that stores the credential (for example a custom key named `Authorization` with the value `Bearer <token>`), so nothing secret is embedded in the definition, unlike an inline header or token.

ref.title: Connect agents to Model Context Protocol servers

questions.stem: A prompt agent definition includes an MCP tool for a remote server that exposes 12 tools. The tool definition sets only `type`, `server_label`, and `server_url`; it doesn't specify `allowed_tools` or `require_approval`. For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: The agent can call any of the 12 tools that the server exposes.
Before a tool on the server runs, the response contains an `mcp_approval_request` output item.
To let a requested call proceed, the application must create a new conversation and resend the user's prompt.

questions.explanation: When `allowed_tools` is omitted, the agent can use every tool that the server exposes; a list of names is needed to restrict access. `require_approval` defaults to `always`, so each call first surfaces an `mcp_approval_request` item. The application lets the call proceed by sending an `mcp_approval_response` item (with `approval_request_id` and `approve`) that continues the same exchange, not by starting over.

questions.stem: A prompt agent uses an MCP tool that is configured with `require_approval` set to `always`. A human reviewer must see the server, tool name, and arguments before each call runs. You need to submit the reviewer's decision so that the agent can continue. Complete the Python code.
questions.explanation: When approval is required, the response output contains an `mcp_approval_request` item with the server label, tool name, and arguments. You answer with an `mcp_approval_response` item whose `approval_request_id` is the request item's `id` and whose `approve` flag carries the decision. `function_call_output` and `call_id` belong to function calling, and `tool_outputs` comes from the classic runs API. Current doc samples submit the approval with `conversation=conversation.id` rather than `previous_response_id`; the items are the same.

questions.stem: An HR team already maintains an Azure AI Search index that has searchable text fields, vector fields, and a semantic configuration. A prompt agent must ground its answers on this index and return citations. Each query must combine keyword and vector retrieval and then apply semantic reranking. You want the least development effort. What should you configure?
options: The Azure AI Search tool with `query_type` set to `vector_semantic_hybrid`
The Azure AI Search tool with `query_type` set to `vector_simple_hybrid`
The Azure AI Search tool with `query_type` set to `semantic`
The file search tool with a new vector store that contains the HR policy files
questions.explanation: The Azure AI Search tool queries an existing index through a project connection. `vector_semantic_hybrid` is the hybrid + semantic option: keyword plus vector retrieval followed by semantic reranking. `vector_simple_hybrid` is hybrid (vector + keyword) without the semantic ranker, and `semantic` omits the vector query. File search would re-ingest the documents into a separate vector store, which is more effort and ignores the existing index. Since November 2026 the docs title this tool Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search) index.
